papers.title_en: Where the Evidence Lives: Measuring Privacy and Diagnosability of Exported AI-Agent Traces
papers.authors: Chang Xu, Hao Wang, Gedi Zhou, Junyuan Tan
papers.evidence: 衡量导出的AI智能体执行轨迹的隐私性与可诊断性
papers.tldr: AI智能体的执行轨迹能帮助定位故障，但直接共享会泄露客户身份；传统脱敏在抹去身份的同时可能删掉修复所需证据。作者构建可执行基准，在多租户合成工作流中量化导出轨迹暴露什么、诊断程序还能修复什么，并比较两种导出策略。结果显示比较事实与执行域内伪名都能保留原有修复能力，后者在42个故障案例中全部修复正确。该基准可同时评测隐私泄露与可诊断性，并暴露行计数这一残留侧信道。
papers.abstract_en: Execution traces help diagnose AI-agent failures, but sharing them can expose customer identities. For example, detecting that an agent handled the wrong customer's records requires knowing whether the records belong to the requested customer, but not necessarily knowing who that customer is. Our executable benchmark measures what a trace export reveals and whether a proposed repair restores the correct output in synthetic multi-tenant workflows. Conventional redaction can remove evidence needed for repair while leaving encoded identifiers recoverable. Two exports preserve ownership comparisons by reporting the match as a comparison fact or by using pseudonyms consistent within each execution. Both preserve the original diagnostic program's repairs. The tested identifier matchers identify no requested customer from either export. An independently written program produces correct outputs on 39 of 42 faulty cases with comparison facts and on all 42 with execution-scoped pseudonyms. Row counts still expose identities. With prior knowledge of customers' row counts, an attacker uniquely identifies the requested customer in 97 of 240 executions under each of the 15 export policies. Removing selected counters from the comparison-fact export stops this attack and preserves the original program's repairs. The benchmark lets engineers test what their diagnostic program can repair and what an attacker can still infer from the same export.

papers.title_en: DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
papers.authors: Hanlin Tian, Sihan Zhu, Zhao Yang, Yuxiang Wang, Zhiquan Hu, Yu Mi, Hongquan Zhu, Qiufei Hu
papers.evidence: 带精确最小动作下界的交互智能体轨迹级评估
papers.tldr: 现有智能体基准只看最终状态是否正确，无法区分高效取证与遍历环境，也无法区分差一步与走弯路。DetourBench 将任务建模为有限部分可观察转移系统，用穷举搜索算出全信息最少动作数 L0 与精确剩余工作量 R_T。在 375 个评估回合中，成功率 58.7%–96.0%，条件达成率 0.803–0.890 且对模型排序不同。该基准开源实例、oracle 见证与评测框架，实现轨迹级可解释评估。
papers.abstract_en: Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists.   We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

papers.title_en: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
papers.authors: Jonathan Ullrich, Julien Siebert, Michael Kläs, Adam Trendowicz, Andreas Jedlitschka
papers.evidence: 将可观测的智能体轨迹作为软件质量保证证据进行分析
papers.tldr: 自主软件代理在有限人工监督下规划、实现和测试软件，其隐含假设可能不被最终代码与通过测试暴露。本文提出把可观测的代理轨迹同软件与代理规格、AI生成产物结合，作为针对性质量保证的证据，优先审查高影响决策并诊断其与软件问题的关联。工业经验支持该思路，现有执行记录和初步分析使其可行，但轨迹本身不足以证明决策合理、结果可接受或修复有效。贡献在于为评审、诊断和持续质量改进提供证据框架，并讨论何时更简单的QA方法已足够。
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous software agents increasingly plan, implement, and test software with limited human oversight. Their decisions may introduce implicit assumptions that final code and passing tests do not adequately expose. We propose analyzing observable agent trajectories alongside software and agent specifications and AI generated artifacts as evidence for targeted quality assurance. The aim is to prioritize consequential decisions for scrutiny, investigate their possible contribution to software problems, and inform improvements to specifications and development practices. Industrial experience motivates the idea; available execution records and preliminary analysis methods make it plausible. However, trajectories alone do not establish that decisions are justified, outcomes acceptable, or corrective changes effective. We ask how this evidence can support review, diagnosis, and continuous quality improvement, and when simpler QA approaches suffice. Perspectives from requirements engineering, verification and validation, agent systems, causal inference, empirical software engineering, and human factors could help develop and evaluate the idea.

papers.title_en: TRACE-MAS: Diagnosing and Repairing Collaboration Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Zekai Chen, Yihan Sun, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu, Xinmo Jin, Yinlin Zhu, Haodong Lu, Xuaner Chen, Rong-Hua Li
papers.evidence: 从良性智能体轨迹学习正常执行模式以检测并修复故障
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体系统的故障常源于智能体间交互，现有防护多停留在智能体级异常检测，难以定位真实根因。TRACE-MAS从良性轨迹学习正常协作模式，检测状态变化、消息转换与任务依赖演化偏差，并用源感知归因锁定责任执行元素、选择最小干预修复协作。在五个MAS基准上，根因定位准确率提升60.2%，任务恢复也稳定增益。该工作将MAS保障推进到更细粒度的交互级诊断与修复。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. Existing MAS safeguards mainly perform agent-level anomaly detection, which becomes insufficient when failures originate from agent interactions and detected anomalies do not necessarily reveal their true sources. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{TRACE-MAS}, a finer-grained framework for diagnosing and repairing MAS failures. TRACE-MAS learns normal collaborative execution patterns from benign trajectories and detects deviations in agent state changes, message transitions, and task dependency evolutions. It further identifies responsible execution elements through source-aware attribution and selects minimal interventions to restore collaboration while preserving task-critical capabilities. Experiments on five MAS benchmarks demonstrate that TRACE-MAS significantly improves root-cause localization accuracy by \textbf{60.2}\% and achieves consistent gains in task recovery over strong MAS safeguards.

papers.title_en: ProbeAgent: Principled Diagnosis of Agent Failures in Verifiable Environments
papers.authors: Yue Huang, Yuchen Ma, Shuhang Lin, Yuyang Wu, Zixuan Weng, Zixiang Xu, Xiangqi Wang, Yuexing Hao, Yujun Zhou, Yue Zhao, Olexandr Isayev, Stefan Feuerriegel, Xiangliang Zhang
papers.evidence: 通过分析失败轨迹诊断agent故障
papers.tldr: 智能体失败诊断常只看最终回答，难以区分任务难度与跨任务重复错误。ProbeAgent 自动构建可执行测试，对失败轨迹提出原因并生成保留该原因、改变上下文的新任务，以验证错误是否复现。它进一步聚类相似原因，生成可区分的失败模式描述。在22种配置、10个基准的1244次失败上产出536条描述，人工接受率90.0%，表明其能细粒度定位并验证智能体失败。
papers.abstract_en: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. An agent acts over multiple steps in a changing environment, so diagnosing its failures requires more than inspecting the final response of a large language model (LLM). The same unsuccessful outcome can arise from task difficulty or from an error the agent repeats across tasks. We introduce ProbeAgent, an automated framework that discovers agent failures, tests their proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes. Starting from benchmark tasks, ProbeAgent builds executable tests and validates them using reference solutions, automated checks, and review of the task requirements. For each failed trajectory, it explains the error and constructs new tasks that preserve the suspected cause while changing the surrounding context. Running the agent on these tasks tests whether the same error recurs. ProbeAgent then groups failures with similar causes and generates descriptions that distinguish their errors. This process connects explanations of individual failures to executable tests and descriptions of shared failure modes. We evaluate ProbeAgent across 22 agent configurations using tasks from 10 benchmarks, collecting 1,244 failures and producing 536 failure-mode descriptions. These descriptions distinguish specific errors within broad outcomes such as incomplete work, including planning without acting and stopping before delivering a file. In human evaluation, annotators accept 90.0% of assigned descriptions and correctly reject 83.3% of similar alternatives, supporting the accuracy and specificity of the discovered failure modes.

papers.title_en: Beyond Clumsy Agentic Tool Calling: How Cueing and Spotting Make the Difference
papers.authors: Xindi Yang, Yan Liu, Jiajun Sun
papers.evidence: 监控LLM智能体的工具使用轨迹与多步绕路
papers.tldr: LLM任务型智能体常忽略执行反馈、重复无效工具调用或陷入多轮绕路。作者提出在线中间件ToolPulse，在调用前监测提议、执行后检查反馈，并用状态规则、语义序列与交互相似度提供提示。在SWE-agent三模型、90个修复任务1350条轨迹上，有效触发后61.6-90.9%出现实质响应，简洁提醒总体最佳。研究区分触发、停止与纠正，显示运行时辅助有效但行为调整未必带来修复收益。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based task-oriented agents depend on tools to interact with their environments, but may overlook execution feedback, repeat ineffective calls, or persist with unproductive strategies. These behaviors can hinder agents' ability to use tools autonomously and sustain task progress. We characterize tool-use symptoms at two temporal granularities: local clumsy tool-use behaviors and tool-use detours spanning multiple interactions. Towards greater autonomy in tool use, we present ToolPulse, an online middleware supporting autonomous tool use through cueing and spotting. ToolPulse tracks execution state and temporal interaction patterns, monitoring proposed calls before dispatch and inspecting execution feedback prior to the agent resumes reasoning. It combines state-based rules, semantic sequence analysis, and interaction-feature similarity to identify intervention opportunities and provide verbal reminders, structured feedback, or context-specific advice from auxiliary models. Our process-oriented evaluation distinguishes trigger validity, behavioral cessation, and substantive correction alongside task outcomes and resource costs. Using SWE-agent with three backbone models, we evaluate 1,350 trajectories on 90 Python, C++, and Java bug-fix tasks, comparing unassisted execution with four assistance strategies. Substantive responses follow 61.6-90.9% of valid triggers for tool-use detours. Concise reminders achieve the highest observed aggregate substantive-response rate; more elaborate assistance offers symptom-dependent benefits and can be less effective. Aggregate repair outcomes remain close to baseline, with token savings in selected settings. These findings support proactive runtime assistance for autonomous tool use. The gap between behavioral adjustment and aggregate repair gains calls for careful decisions on intervention timing and assistance strategy in autonomous agents.

papers.title_en: When Facts Change, Which Decisions Break? Dependency-Aware Context Graphs for Agents
papers.evidence: 从真实agent读取轨迹中提取依赖图以修复决策
papers.tldr: 当观测事实变化时，智能体需识别并修复依赖该事实的决策，同时保留不受影响的输出。本文基于真实读取轨迹提取字段级依赖图，在三个可执行工作流域、四次连续更新、120个工作流上对比全量重算、滚动摘要、词法检索、轨迹依赖与验证上界。结果显示轨迹图能减少复核决策与估计总成本，但遗漏替代支撑会降低完整计划正确率。增强版目录感知图在部分模型上追平全上下文正确率并降本约4%。
papers.abstract_en: When an observed fact changes, an agent must identify and repair the decisions that depend on it while preserving unaffected outputs. We investigate the reliability-cost trade-off of field-level dependency graphs extracted from actual agent read traces. A controlled benchmark spans three executable workflow domains and four successive updates, with independent imperative and expression-based references. Across 120 workflows, two models and two repeated runs, we compare full recomputation, rolling summary memory, lexical retrieval, trace-extracted dependencies and verified dependency upper bounds. Trace-derived graphs reduce reviewed decisions and estimated total cost, but omitted alternative supports and missing repair context can reduce complete-plan correctness. Paired ablations isolate the effects of edge deletion, spurious edges, transitive propagation and context scope. An exploratory enhancement supplies the existing record ID/field directory during extraction without revealing unread values or reference edges. We evaluate this enhancement on 60 fresh workflows with two repeats per model. On this fresh set, the directory-aware graph matches observed full-context complete-plan correctness for gpt-6.1-sol (100%) with an estimated 4.0% total-cost reduction, but reaches only 84.8% versus 99.6% for gpt-6-luna. The results distinguish potential dependency impact from actual decision invalidity and show why selective repair must be evaluated with both executable correctness and full memory-processing cost. The evidence concerns explicit procedural workflows; broad real-world agent-memory generalization remains untested.

papers.title_en: Securing and Auditing Long-Horizon LLM Agents: State-Transfer Auditing and Controls in the Agent Harness
papers.evidence: 在执行框架中通过状态转移追踪审计长时智能体
papers.tldr: 长程LLM智能体依赖执行框架在工作上下文、会话历史、持久记忆与外部环境间转移状态，但现有轨迹日志不记录跨边界内容，导致注入、丢失约束和回滚不完整难归因。本文提出状态转移审计架构，在每个转移边界定义最小哈希链记录，区分确定性检查与模型语义检查。参考中间件在240条多步故障注入轨迹上定位根因，捕获仅生命周期/工具日志漏掉的跨转移违规，确定性开销为微秒级。该工作把审计记录与运行时控制统一，为智能体安全与恢复提供可落地基础。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon LLM agents across codebases, web browsers, and enterprise infrastructure rely on an execution harness to move state between the working context, session history, persistent memory, and external environment. While conventional execution traces log model prompts and tool calls, critical security and reliability failures occur during state transfers: a transfer can admit unchecked content (indirect prompt injections, unverified memory writes), rewrite state lossily (context compaction dropping user constraints, memory consolidation stripping source authority), or restore state incompletely (workspace rollbacks leaving aborted KV state active on the inference server). Because current traces omit what crosses these boundaries, failure attribution and runtime monitors fail on multi-step trajectories. We present a state-transfer audit architecture for the agent harness. At each transfer boundary, we define an audit point specifying the minimal hash-chained record the harness emits, separating low-overhead deterministic checks from model-based semantic checks and binding internal context, memory, and inference-server cache state to external actions. We show that the same transfer records required for causal failure attribution supply the durable state needed by runtime security controls, including least-privilege capabilities, replay-resistant authorization outside the prompt, information flow control, obligation monitors, and transactional recovery across multi-agent and infrastructure pipelines. Finally, we analyze multimodal GUI adaptations and implement and evaluate a reference harness middleware across 240 multi-step fault-injection trajectories, showing that transfer records localize root causes and catch cross-transfer violations missed by lifecycle and tool-only logs at microsecond deterministic overhead.

papers.title_en: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
papers.authors: K. R. Jayaram, Vatche Isahagian, Aswath Vaithinathan Aravindan, Vinod Muthusamy, Punleuk Oum, Gaodan Fang, Michal Ulewicz, Gegi Thomas, Evelyn Duesterwald
papers.evidence: 从智能体轨迹中挖掘经验以构建自蒸馏记忆
papers.tldr: 长程LLM智能体常重复犯错，本文提出自蒸馏记忆流水线：从自身轨迹挖掘1-3条lessons，再合并为带计数的guidelines，推理时注入全部或子集。AppWorld上，强模型DeepSeek-V3.2用191条guideline提升任务完成+9.5、场景完成+16.1；弱模型gpt-oss-120b从39.9%升至全量51.2%，约29条子集达55.4%。结论是合适记忆量取决于模型，并总结部署失效与建议。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. At inference the agent receives either all guidelines or a selected subset. The pipeline ships in the open-source altk-evolve library and is deployed in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate platform. We report what we learned building, measuring, and productizing it. Our primary instrument is the AppWorld benchmark, across models spanning 40--92\% baseline task completion. The central finding is that the right amount of memory is a property of the model, not the memory. A strong model keeps improving as guidelines are added. DeepSeek-V3.2 gains +9.5 points of task completion and +16.1 points of scenario completion with its full 191-guideline set. A weak model gains less from the same full set than from a small selected subset. gpt-oss-120b starts at 39.9\% task completion. It reaches 51.2\% with all 199 of its guidelines but 55.4\% (mean of two runs) with a selected subset of about 29. Around that result we report what went wrong: a high-support guideline that backfired, provenance silently dropped during consolidation, a swallowed API error that failed every task while producing a plausible log, and a baseline confound that nearly produced a misleading comparison with a prior method. We distill these into recommendations for teams deploying agent memory.

papers.authors: Yicheng Cai, Taegyu Kim, Peng Liu
papers.evidence: 利用轨迹日志回溯agent安全事件
papers.tldr: 智能体应用加速部署，但安全事件回溯面临轨迹日志与代码函数调用的语义鸿沟，人工定位入侵入口代价高且易遗漏。Origin构建跨层依赖图CLDG，将区域推断函数与低层污点传播变量关联，并提供查询语言和区域推断算法。在5个流行智能体应用的8起攻击事件中，分析者用Origin提交少量查询即正确识别全部CEP。该工作降低了代码审查成本，为智能体应用安全事件溯源提供了可查询、可操作的CEP定位工具。
papers.abstract_en: Agent applications are increasingly deployed, yet agent-specific attacks pose real threats to them. Upon a security incident, organizations backtrack to identify the CEP (compromise entry point), remediate the damage, and prevent its recurrence. The main artifacts available for backtracking are trajectory logs, which record agent functionalities, and source code; app(lication)-specific function call logs are often fairly limited. However, trajectory logs are at the agent functionality abstraction layer, while the CEP candidates are function calls at the app code execution layer. Due to this semantic gap, the analyst needs to manually inspect the relevant code for each CEP candidate to infer its corresponding agent functionality. In this work, we present Origin, a backtracking tool for the analyst to submit a small number of queries to identify CEPs that existing tools cannot provide. Our approach poses two challenges: (1) define the intermediate abstraction that captures the mapping relationships between the two semantic layers; (2) determine the region-to-variable mapping for constructing the cross-layer graph defined in the intermediate abstraction. Each region is a specific group of agent functionalities. Origin addresses the challenges by (1) the cross-layer dependency graph (CLDG) that connects region-inferred functions at the semantic level to the variables in the low-level taint propagation subgraph, plus the associated query language, and (2) the region inference algorithm. Case studies on five popular agent applications across eight attack incidents show that an analyst using Origin correctly identifies all the CEPs.

papers.title_en: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
papers.authors: Deyang Kong, Zhaoyi Li, Sijian Ren, Ying Wei, Defu Lian, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye
papers.evidence: 分析蒸馏如何重塑ReAct推理、动作与观察轨迹
papers.tldr: 在线策略蒸馏（OPD）可向语言模型智能体迁移专项能力，但其跨域重塑ReAct交互模式的机制尚不清晰。本文在数学、ALFWorld和τ²-bench上分析推理、动作与观察获取的变化，并利用教师偏好变化筛选位置进行选择性OPD。结果显示通用推理监督使数学工具尝试从70.4%降至14.4%、准确率从16.7%升至38.0%，而ALFWorld监督会使τ²准确率从41.5%降至6.6%；保留前95%位置可将τ²准确率从11.5%提升至29.9%。
papers.abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and $τ^2$-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces $τ^2$-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises $τ^2$ accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

papers.title_en: HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
papers.authors: Chirag Goel, Jacob Lavoie, Amirhossein Naghshzan, Jordan Bannister, Marzia Nouri, Mehar Bhatia, Matt Harris, Siva Reddy, Arsène Fansi Tchango, Gaétan Marceau Caron
papers.evidence: 面向agent记忆系统的整体性评估框架
papers.tldr: 记忆系统让AI智能体跨交互持久保存信息，却带来不当披露、难纠删、过度保留和投毒风险，现有评估多只看性能与效率。HEAMS把记忆系统视为用户持久信息托管者，将性能、效率、安全、隐私和用户主权转为显式期望，并构建开源基准与可包裹任意系统的治理层。用MilaMem原型全基准比较发现，无系统领先所有性能基准，强性能可与差隐私、主权和安全并存。治理影响显著：召回策略减少不当披露但牺牲有用性，召回与保留策略均提升抗投毒，说明仅性能效率评估不足。
papers.abstract_en: Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities of agent memory systems as explicit behavioural desiderata spanning performance, efficiency, security, privacy, and user sovereignty. Second, we assemble a benchmark suite that covers these desiderata and acknowledge the gaps that remain. Third, we develop MilaMem, a prototype memory system, and a governance layer that can wrap any memory system, enabling controlled study of memory system design choices. Fourth, we compare memory systems across the full HEAMS benchmark suite. We find that no memory system leads every performance benchmark, and strong performance scores may coexist with poor privacy, user-sovereignty, and security scores. Governance strongly influences results: recall policies can reduce inappropriate disclosure at a cost in helpfulness, while both recall and retention policies improve poisoning resistance. Performance and efficiency benchmarks alone therefore cannot reveal how well a memory system meets its responsibilities. Code: https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams

papers.title_en: Synapse: Optimizing Natural-Language Agent Skills through Program Repair
papers.authors: Lijuan Li, Zhenpeng Chen, Chenxi Zhang, Yihao Huang, Yang Liu, Chong Wang
papers.evidence: 结合执行轨迹与控制流依赖定位agent技能中的故障
papers.tldr: LLM智能体可通过优化自然语言技能提升任务表现，但执行反馈难以定位应修改的指令及潜在回归。Synapse将技能优化建模为基于局部程序视图的生成—验证修复：编译器把可识别技能构件转为源链接SkIR，并结合执行轨迹、控制流与依赖关系定位故障、生成类型化变异、筛选相关测试。在DocVQA与LiveMath、三种执行模型下，其成功率较SkillOpt提升3.74–4.54与2.40–4.00个百分点，并在六个设置中优于Trace2Skill和SkillBoost。消融显示SkIR修复与结构关系测试筛选能减少回归，为自然语言技能自动修复提供可验证方案。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents can improve task performance by optimizing reusable natural-language skills without updating model parameters. Execution feedback reveals failures but does not directly identify which instructions to edit, which related instructions matter, or which tasks an edit may break. We propose Synapse, which casts skill optimization as generate-and-validate repair over a partial program view. A deterministic compiler translates recognized skill constructs into SkIR, a source-linked intermediate representation, while retaining other requirements in the text. Synapse combines execution traces with control-flow and dependence relations to localize faults, propose typed mutations, and select related repair tests, including previously passing ones. Each mutation is written back to its mapped source span and recompiled; validation determines acceptance. Every accepted patch yields a well-formed skill and preserves untargeted instruction spans. Under a one-hop-local execution assumption, selected tests include every test an edit can affect. On DocVQA and LiveMath with three execution models, Synapse improves task success rates over SkillOpt by 3.74-4.54 and 2.40-4.00 percentage points, respectively, and outperforms Trace2Skill and SkillBoost in all six settings. Replacing SkIR-based repair and its test screening with constrained text editing screened only on failing tests lowers DocVQA success rates by 2.40 and 2.67 percentage points for two models. In two recorded repair runs, structural relations add tests for 23 of 37 patches; in one repair, a test added through a control-flow relation exposes a regression missed by coverage of the edited instruction.

papers.title_en: SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
papers.authors: Tae Soo Kim, Tongshuang Wu, Juho Kim
papers.evidence: 将记录的agent会话作为轨迹数据回放评估
papers.tldr: 记录用户与编程智能体的真实会话可用于评估，但换用新智能体后轨迹变化会使原始用户回复失效，直接回放不可行。SWE-WhatIf 通过建模用户意图、满足标准及其触发条件，构建能适应未见智能体动作且扎根录制的用户模拟器。在89个真实会话中，其生成回复最接近真实用户，并在避免用户曾反对动作上取得66.3%胜率。该工作还用于排序五个LLM编程智能体，并显示回放自身会话会改变多数用户排名与后续使用。
papers.abstract_en: Recorded sessions between users and coding agents offer a way to evaluate how agents complete real-world tasks and interact with users. However, these sessions cannot simply be replayed with new agents, because recorded user replies may no longer apply when an agent takes a different trajectory. We introduce SWE-WhatIf, which replays recorded sessions with new agents by modeling the user's intents, the criteria for satisfying them, and the conditions under which they arise. Using this model, a user simulator generates replies that adapt to unseen agent turns while remaining grounded in the recording. Across 89 real-world sessions, SWE-WhatIf generated the replies most similar to those of real users and matched the strongest baseline when sessions were rewritten. To test adaptation, we replay sessions with agents instructed to avoid or repeat actions that the recorded user pushed back on. SWE-WhatIf produced the highest win rate for avoiding these actions (66.3%), significantly above chance. We further demonstrate its utility by ranking five LLMs as coding agents, where the highest-ranked model depended on how users specified and developed their intents, and a study with 16 users, where replaying their own sessions changed 14 participants' rankings and informed their future agent use.

papers.title_en: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
papers.evidence: 跨基准评估agent可靠性的统计框架
papers.tldr: 针对复杂多工具环境中LLM智能体可靠性评估受任务异质性与执行随机性干扰的问题，论文提出场景—实例—样本的层次化统计框架，并为平均通过率、pass@k与passhat^k给出不确定度估计。作者推导无偏估计量的有限样本方差，构造层次不确定度传播，并将其与粗粒化过程对应。该框架可分离执行噪声与任务异质性，揭示不同聚合层级下的性能结构，为生产环境可靠性评估提供系统方法。
papers.abstract_en: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

papers.title_en: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
papers.authors: Gunjan Siddharth, Sanjana Garai, Utsav Shekhar, Prakhar Jain, Sarvam Maheshwari, Balaji Ganesan, Avirup Saha, Seema Nagar, Pratik Mishra, Felix George, Suranjana Samanta, Harshit Kumar, Mudit Verma, Prateeti Mohapatra, Ravi Jagannathan, Amit Paradkar, Sameep Mehta, Pratibha Moogi
papers.evidence: 为智能体加入分析埋点，使其模型与工具调用可被追踪观测
papers.tldr: ITOps 可观测性产品需要整合多工具、多系统的数据，为此作者提出 ITOps Observability Studio——一个多模态多智能体系统，用协作式 AI 智能体编排可观测性工作流。系统采用三层架构，包含智能体间通信、由 LLM 驱动的数据访问、模式操作与可视化专用智能体，以及统一工具集成，支持自然语言转 GraphQL、Schema 生成与映射、追踪数据生命周期管理和可靠性工程多工具工作流。各智能体在各自基准上评估，公开基准上的查询生成与路由表现良好，数据生命周期智能体可解决多数场景；评估还暴露了提示、解析器与服务栈联合测试才出现的缺陷并给出修复。
papers.abstract_en: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. Query generation on a public benchmark and routing work well with a current open model, and the data lifecycle management agent solves most of its scenarios. The evaluation exposed defects that only appear when prompts, parsers and serving stacks are tested together, and we report them together with their fixes.

papers.title_en: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
papers.authors: Yerin Nam, Minkyung Cho, MinKyu Kim, SeungWoo Song, Hangyeol Yoo, Jihyo Kim, KyungTae Lim
papers.evidence: 用于评估GUI智能体的证据驱动基准
papers.tldr: GUI agent 常以网页任务完成率评估，但表面成功可能掩盖答案缺乏导航中所见证据支撑的问题。作者提出 EVIDENT 基准，含 220 个英韩真实任务，覆盖语义、上下文与视觉 grounding，并用 TSR、ESR、GSR 分离表面完成与证据支撑成功。实验显示商业与开源 agent 在两类成功间差距显著，上下文与视觉任务尤甚。该工作表明现有评估会高估 agent 可靠性，需同时考察是否验证证据。
papers.abstract_en: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.
